# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 exporting manufacturers). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| supplier_diversity | Number of distinct input suppliers (standardized), 2021-2022 |
| export_growth_2023 | Export value growth in 2023 (percent index) |
| log_sales_2020 | Log sales, 2020 |
| years_exporting_2020 | Years since first export, standardized, 2020 |
| export_growth_2020 | Export value growth in 2020, standardized |
| buyer_rating_2023 | Average rating from foreign buyers, 2023 |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| product_group | Sector: durables / nondurables |
| inventory_days_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| foreign_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_imported_inputs_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| port_distance_km | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| certified_iso | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| debt_ratio_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of supplier diversification on export growth?

Approach: OLS of export_growth_2023 on supplier_diversity with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I control for firm size, firm age, the pre-period value of the outcome and buyer_rating_2023, which captures an important determinant of the outcome, and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on supplier_diversity is -2.219 (SE 0.219, p = 0.0000, N = 1960).

Conclusion: negative effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

content.text: Without the post-treatment control, the effect is about 0.05 (null). The negative sign appears only after conditioning on buyer_rating_2023, which is a collider/mediator.

input.content: {"decision":"reject","reason":"The negative estimate (-2.2) comes from controlling for buyer_rating_2023, a 2023 post-treatment variable (mediator/collider). Without it, with pre-period controls only or with the full set of pre-period covariates, the supplier_diversity coefficient is about 0.05 (SE 0.25), which is null. The 'negative effect' conclusion is an artifact of the bad control."}

content.text:
I rejected the report and wrote `verdict.json` with that decision. The "negative effect" conclusion comes from a control that shouldn't be in the model.

The analyst controlled for `buyer_rating_2023`, which is measured in 2023, after the supplier diversification period (2021–2022). It is likely affected by the treatment, so conditioning on it biases the estimate. It correlates 0.49 with `supplier_diversity` and 0.55 with `export_growth_2023`.

I re-ran the regression with HC1 errors in several specifications:

| Specification | Coefficient on `supplier_diversity` | SE |
|---|---|---|
| No controls | 1.78 | 0.25 |
| Pre-period controls only (size, years exporting, 2020 export growth) | 0.057 | 0.246 |
| Analyst's spec (adds `buyer_rating_2023`) | −2.41 | 0.23 |
| All pre-period covariates, region, listed and product group | 0.051 | 0.247 |

The analyst reports −2.219 because they also trimmed the outcome by 1%, which I did not do. Once the 2023 rating is dropped, the effect is about zero.

I could not read `analysis.py`, so I haven't checked the analyst's code. I rebuilt the specifications from the report's description instead.
